display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
After discovery, before research, architecture and planning
Project-wide now. Feature detail just in time
Size is computed from the entities, roles, screens, endpoints and rules
A line count is an output, never a target

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Generators are code. Most cells cost no tokens
They emit only what exists
Permission: entity, action, role. Fields: type, limits, who sets them
Lifecycle: states, transitions, who, side effects
Screen states. Every control: action, disabled, feedback
Endpoint failures. Boundaries: before, at, after. Zero, one, many, max
Concurrency of two actors. Lists: sort, page, search, empty, huge
Deletion and retention. Notifications. Formatting of dates and money
Thousands of identical cells collapse to one scoped rule

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Where does this cell's value come from?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: explicit. Full credit

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: derived. Full credit

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
defaulted. Full credit. Listed in Chosen for you
Code fills these before any model sees the cell

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
proposed by spec-expander. Full credit if risk is low
Medium risk goes to review

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Status asked, not a basis. Through the interrogation guard

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Each cell is one EARS item: ID, pattern, text, basis,
source decisions, risk, and an oracle sketch
Ubiquitous: the system shall. Event: when. State: while
Unwanted: if, then. Optional: where the feature is included
The planner later turns the oracle into a check

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Contradiction check. Code first

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: conflicts_with and requires on catalog values

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Find combinations that are impossible together,
and the smallest set of decisions to change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The same IDs, compared. A denied permission with a visible button

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Intervals and order. A cutoff after the kitchen already needs the list

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A cheap model, only for pairs that share an entity, rule or screen
and that layers 1 to 4 did not decide. Conflict, compatible, or unclear

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: How were the two items chosen?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The Manager keeps the option that preserves more explicit decisions
Reason recorded. Listed in Chosen for you

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The explicit one wins. The other changes. Dependents are rechecked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Ask the developer, with both quotes

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
100 percent info: every required cell has a valid basis,
no unresolved contradiction, no critical question open
The screen counts explicit, derived, defaulted, proposed and asked
Proposed items can be accepted, edited or rejected
Generators and layers 1 to 4 are free. The expander is Mid, per feature,
only for cells that need judgement. This spends the paperwork budget

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A later decision regenerates only the cells that cited it
A proposed value stays labeled, including in the brief and the plan preview
No elaboration or policy: propose or ask, and log the gap for the meta-lab

svg.text: Spec expansion — every cell filled, then checked
